critical.issue: Diacritic-insensitive matching fails: 'PT Nestle Indonesia' NOT detected as duplicate of seeded 'PT Nestlé Indonesia'. The `norm()` helper strips 'é' via `[^a-z0-9]` so the two normalized strings differ ('ptnestlindonesia' vs 'ptnestleindonesia') and neither is a substring of the other. Requirements explicitly require this exact case to trigger the duplicate alert.

rca of the issue: Root cause of duplicate-detection miss: `norm(s) = re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]', '', s.lower())` removes the character 'é' entirely since it is not in [a-z0-9], producing 'ptnestlindonesia' from 'PT Nestlé Indonesia'. Input 'PT Nestle Indonesia' produces 'ptnestleindonesia'. Substring check fails because of the extra 'e'. Fix: import unicodedata; s2 = unicodedata.normalize('NFKD', s).encode('ascii','ignore').decode('ascii'); then apply lowercase + alnum-strip. This maps 'é' -> 'e' before stripping, so both inputs normalize to 'ptnestleindonesia' → 100% match. Also apply to the /api/partners search regex path or add a normalized_name field to partners to enable diacritic-insensitive substring search.
